A response plot, a complex root and an optimizer's best point answer different
questions. This guide connects the current public API to the shared physical
program and explains what Hint, explicit discovery, tracking and local derivatives
mean. The implementation remains `CONVERGING`; this page does not establish
strict Example regression coverage, independent accuracy or a stable release.
The [Runtime Contract](../v1-runtime-contract.qmd#typed-direct-quantity-catalog)
owns the detailed quantity and failure definitions.

## Decide which quantity you need

A minimum of $|S_{ij}(\omega)|$ or $|Z_{ij}(\omega)|$ sampled at real frequencies
is a magnitude notch. It need not be an exact zero at a real frequency. A
transfer zero is a root of the declared **complex** S, Y or Z entry under its
selected View and loading. A pole or resonance solves another equation and
must not be substituted for that zero merely because its frequency is close.

| Declaration | Question |
|---|---|
| `DirectSolveSpec` or `ResponseElementSpec` | What is the response at the requested real frequencies? |
| `DiagonalRootSpec` / `OperatorElementRootSpec` | Where does the selected Schur-operator entry vanish? |
| `HybridizedPoleSpec` | Where does the selected coupled pole equation close? |
| `TransferZeroSpec` | Where does this ordered S/Y/Z transfer numerator vanish while its denominator remains admissible? |
| `ResidueNormalizedCouplingSpec` | What local coupling follows from the declared certified branch roots and slopes? |

Coordinates and direction matter: `output_coordinate` is the row and
`input_coordinate` the column. The same physical Plan can yield different
selected quantities after different loads, compensation, coordinate transforms
or retained boundaries. Retaining an unported node does not make it a Port or
silently remove its load. Start with [simulation conventions](../concepts/simulation-conventions.qmd)
and [Views](../concepts/compilation-coordinates-and-network-views.qmd).

## Frequency units and the selected equation

Public Hint/anchor inputs are frequency Quantities. The numerical equation uses
angular frequency $\omega=2\pi f$ in rad/s and the $\exp(-i\omega t)$ convention.
The complex `zero` or `root` and the public Hz `frequency` field are distinct
projections; a display-unit conversion must not silently add or remove $2\pi$.
With this time convention, an actually decaying pole has
$\operatorname{Im}\omega<0$. Current JAX hybrid-pole closure admits
$\operatorname{Im}\omega\le0$, including a lossless real-axis root. This is not
an automatic extra passivity filter on all scalar or transfer zeros.

For an admitted fixed linear nodal model, put $s=-i\omega$. The loaded operator
and selected intrinsic Schur operator have the form

$$
Q=K+sG+s^2C,\qquad
F=Q_{RR}-Q_{RE}Q_{EE}^{-1}Q_{ER},\qquad
Y=\frac{F}{-i\omega}.
$$

The actual model also preserves its declared series branches, loads, View weights
and corresponding frequency jets. The eliminated solve and its derivative are
part of the same selected-state producer, not independent assemblies. Port
Views use their actual source/load incidence and reference normalization; an
intrinsic formula is not a substitute for a Port response.

For nonzero $\omega$ and invertible selected $F$,

$$
Z_{ij}=(-i\omega)\frac{\operatorname{cof}_{ji}(F)}{\det F}.
$$

The cofactor indices are transposed. Only for a two-coordinate off-diagonal
projection does this simplify to $Z_{21}=i\omega F_{21}/\det F$. A pole spectrum
of $F$ alone is not a catalogue of transmission zeros. See the
[quantity realization](../implementation/direct-poles-zeros-and-operators.qmd)
for the complete loading, Schur and family conventions.

## A Hint is a seed, not a search instruction

With `search=None`, Hint/anchor initializes one local analytic corrector. Newton
updates do not inspect every root below the Hint, select the nearest physical
root, or discover a desired RF notch by definition. A root can lie in another
basin, a candidate can fail its numerical certificate, or the required root can
remain unfound. None of these observations proves that no such root exists.

The current Z-transfer update uses the scaled RF cofactor of the same family
state, $r=\operatorname{cof}_{ji}(F_{\mathrm{eff}})$ with
$F_{\mathrm{eff}}=(-i\omega)Y$. Intrinsic Views reuse their checked $F/F'$;
Port Views use $F'_{\mathrm{eff}}=-iY+(-i\omega)Y'$. This removes an explicit DC
factor from the iteration residual. It does not guarantee the desired positive
frequency basin or change the success definition.

Success still uses the original family/cofactor(Y), full transfer value/slope,
denominator, local simplicity/rank and correction/closure certificates. Y and S
updates retain their own family-entry equations. Existing update limits and
bit-stagnation behavior remain in force. A small correction certificate is not
a forward error bound on the root location; an update count is not a count of
all factors or callbacks. The [root procedure](../implementation/diagonal-root-numerical-procedure.qmd)
and [Runtime Contract](../v1-runtime-contract.qmd) retain those exact rules.

## Declare discovery separately

`RootSearchSpec` is optional on existing root Specs. It requires a method and
exact-tie choice. The caller supplies a real-frequency interval or a positive
factor of the **original authored** Hint. An optional imaginary interval adds
an explicit selection restriction; omission does not invent one.

For authored Hint $h$ and caller factor $k$, the relative positive-RF upper
bound is $kh$. A later baseline/tracked anchor $a$ never replaces $h$ or expands
that region. There is no inferred $h/k$ lower cutoff or automatic sampled grid.
`tie="unavailable"` preserves ambiguity; `tie="source_order"` makes exact ties
follow the declared source order.

| Method | Candidate source and capability |
|---|---|
| `polynomial_transfer_zero` | Qualified intrinsic/non-Port Z with fixed realized mesh, declared pure-inductive sections and frequency-independent K/C/G plus actual loads/View; no caller seeds |
| `finite_seeds` | Caller-supplied ordered nonempty complex-frequency seeds, passed to the original corrector |

Unsupported polynomial capability fails explicitly. A variable resistive section
that happens to evaluate to zero is not automatically a declared pure-inductive
section. There is no hidden method fallback. For the qualified polynomial model,
the provider constructs a dense $2n+1$ SISO Rosenbrock transmission-zero pencil
from the same coefficients and actual input/output. Generalized eig proposals
are not certified roots: defined in-region proposals each pass the original
corrector and certificates in source order before selection.

Selection is nearest-Hint complex-frequency Euclidean distance **among eligible
certified candidates from that declared discovery**. It is not a guarantee of
all continuum roots or the globally nearest physical root. Outside-region
certified candidates retain their outcome and outside-selection fact; failure
to select is reported as not found from the declared trials, not nonexistence.

The caller must author adequate resolution for the intended analysis. Recording
search extent and mesh strategy does not rewrite a sealed Plan or automatically
remesh it. Public `evaluate` has no Optimization fixed-stage mesh override.
Its realized mesh follows the caller's Plan policy; a separate fixed-stage
witness can describe a different discrete problem. See
[electrical resolution](../concepts/electrical-resolution.qmd).

## Use the existing Plan and View

The following function consumes caller-owned declarations and parameters; it
does not author a demonstration circuit or supply an answer seed. A
`NetworkViewRef` belongs to its Run. Pass the existing `ReductionPipeline`
declaration to bind the same View within this new Run, rather than reusing a
foreign Run's reference.

```python
from scnsim import CircuitRun, RootSearchSpec, TransferZeroSpec


def evaluate_notch(*, plan, view_pipeline, input_coordinate,
                   output_coordinate, authored_hint, point):
    spec = TransferZeroSpec(
        anchor=authored_hint,
        family="Z",
        input_coordinate=input_coordinate,
        output_coordinate=output_coordinate,
        search=RootSearchSpec(
            method="polynomial_transfer_zero",
            hint_frequency_factor=10,
            tie="unavailable",
        ),
    )
    run = CircuitRun(plan=plan, storage="memory", precision="float64")
    try:
        view = run.original.reduce(view_pipeline)
        result = run.evaluate(view, spec, parameters=point)
    finally:
        run.close()
    return result
```

The factor is an explicit request choice, not a default. It creates a new request
identity relative to a no-search Spec. Read `result.status`, `result.failure`,
`result.context`, `result.discretization` and `result.benchmark`; when
`result.succeeded`, `result.frequency` is the Hz projection and `result.zero`
is complex angular frequency. Typed numerical failure remains visible;
unexpected transport/native errors propagate. The returned memory Result is
detached and remains readable after close without a saved attempt or `resolve`.

## Track a branch and differentiate locally

Initial discovery establishes anchors. A declared Sweep keeps its original
Plan baseline and point order; explicit single-point search initializes at
that requested point. Optimization establishes original-point anchors under
each declared stage model. Later points use the selected branch and existing
baseline-anchored continuation, not a fresh global search at every parameter.
Completion order does not silently update anchors.

Continuation has its existing failure eligibility and parameter semantics;
not every formation error authorizes a retry. Structured RLGC replacements are
not automatically interpolated by scalar continuation. Every candidate uses
its own checked packet and actual checked Error, not a previous point's Error.

For a locally available simple root equation $g(\theta,\omega)=0$,

$$
\mathrm d\omega=-\frac{g_\theta[\mathrm d\theta]}{g_\omega}.
$$

This derivative belongs to the selected physical branch. It does not differentiate
candidate sorting or the finite Newton history. Actual View/material coefficient
dependence and root-induced frequency dependence remain traced in admitted
second/mixed directions. Frequency-root availability and vector/gauge or
coupling availability can differ; an unavailable derivative is not replaced by
zero or a finite-difference fallback.

`spec.frequency.on(view)` can enter a caller-authored `SensitivitySpec`; its
wrt, JVP direction or VJP weights retain their units and order. The
[Sensitivity guide](sensitivity.qmd) explains partial blocks and normalization.
Raw `PreparedFunction` callables expose local array-only work and status, not
high-level discrete discovery or certified Results. External JAX input/transform
precision is the caller's responsibility; high-level calls own scoped precision.

## Compensation is arithmetic, not branch selection

The represented high/low sparse equation and its fixed correction address
finite-arithmetic residuals under the existing numerical policy. Sparse factors
are callback-local and released before their callback returns; Run caches store
static programs/executables, not factors. First/frequency jets may share ready
RHS work, while tangent, mixed or adjoint equations retain their own actual
performed/status/certificate responsibility.

Compensation cannot choose a Newton basin or create a missing certified root.
If high-channel factorization fails, the correction cannot repair that seed;
this alone does not prove that the total represented operator is singular.
There is no all-device or universally single-factor derivative claim.

## Understand cost and the scope of a fix

| Work | What can happen |
|---|---|
| Compile-only warmup | Compile known candidate/value/linearization signatures; no eig, root correction, factors or successful Result |
| Initial discovery | Acquire coefficients, allocate a dense pencil, run eig and correct each eligible proposal |
| Later branch tracking | Evaluate current coefficients and local correction/eligible continuation, then requested jets |
| Objective/derivative | Apply the same physical quantities and loss, plus the requested local derivative equations |
| Typed API / saved read | Bind/projection/evidence/lifecycle work, or readonly fixed saved-result hydration |

Dense pencil storage grows with matrix dimension; discovery is not a constant-cost
replacement for one sparse local solve. Denominator verification, terminal
certificates, derivative equations, compilation and result construction can also
contribute. Cold preparation, warmup, warm numerical work, complete typed API and
saved lookup are different clocks. Inclusive phase sums are not exclusive costs
and must not be added as if independent. [Benchmark](benchmark.qmd) reports
actual available clocks without executing another calculation.

Reusing a compiled signature does not cache a root catalogue or a native factor.
Consumers that need an actual completed packet/Error or producer Partial tree
remain lazy when that tree is unavailable during warmup. A raw aggregate compile
does not prove a checked consumer hit.

Implementation corrections can address a residual representation, packet/Error
association, admitted higher-order dependence, structural ordinal binding or
precision/callback transport. Those are different from proving a physical model,
a different root's existence, the original whole application workflow, or a
performance target. A source correction is not its own numerical observation;
private collector/setup failures are not automatically solver failures.

For Optimization, CMA-ES can progress past recorded failed candidates. Genuine
L-BFGS-B still needs its actual value/gradient contract. Projected L-BFGS is a
separate value-first reject-aware method: with an accepted real gradient it can
record a failed/unavailable trial and try a smaller feasible step; it cannot
invent an initial direction when that gradient is unavailable. Hybrid stages
retain their explicit strategies, meshes, transitions and comparisons. A lower
cost, or a successfully selected notch, does not establish global optimality,
all targets or an independent physical validation.
